lessons.title: Ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand that 'famille' means family and can identify their own family members
lessons.openingConnection: This is our very first lesson about families! Look at your family photos at home.

mainActivity.description: Family photo sharing circle with visual support
activities: Show diverse family photos and point to 'famille'
Students hold their family photos and say 'ma famille'
Practice maman/papa with gestures and pointing
Family photo walk - students move around showing photos
visualSupports: Large diverse family photos on wall
Hand gestures for maman (rocking baby) and papa (strong arms)
Picture cards showing different family structures

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students with French sounds?
decisionPoints.ifComfortable: Add more vocabulary and encourage repetition
decisionPoints.ifNotComfortable: Focus on listening and gestures, reduce speaking pressure

decisionPoints.question: Do students need visual family photos?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide family photo collection for students without photos
decisionPoints.ifNo: Let students draw quick family pictures if they prefer

decisionPoints.question: Should I use more gestures for comprehension?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Increase TPR with family member actions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Balance gestures with verbal repetition

whenThingsGoWrong.studentOverwhelmed: Switch to just pointing and saying 'famille' together
whenThingsGoWrong.noFamilyPhotos: Use provided diverse family photo collection
whenThingsGoWrong.tooNoise: Move to quiet finger-pointing activity with photos

lessons.closing: Students point to their family photo and whisper 'ma famille' - celebrates diversity
lessons.realWorldConnection: Everyone has a family and can talk about who lives at home

lessons.title: Qui est dans ma famille?
lessons.oneGoal: Students can name 3 basic family members using simple French words
lessons.openingConnection: Yesterday we learned 'famille' - today we learn WHO is in the family!

mainActivity.description: Family member identification with movement and photos
activities: Review maman/papa with yesterday's photos
Introduce frère with tall/short gestures and photo examples
Practice sœur with girl gestures and inclusive examples
Add grand-maman with loving grandma gestures
Family member sorting game with photos
visualSupports: Family member picture cards showing diversity
Height gestures for frère (brother)
Inclusive photos showing different family structures

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for siblings vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifReady: Continue with frère/sœur and let students share about siblings
decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Focus only on parents today, save siblings for tomorrow

decisionPoints.question: Do students need to draw their families first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with 5-minute family drawing, then add vocabulary
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use photos and cards for vocabulary introduction

decisionPoints.question: Should I include different family structures?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Show single parents, step-siblings, adopted families naturally
decisionPoints.ifSensitive: Focus on 'people who love us' rather than traditional labels

materials: Large chart paper for family sorting

whenThingsGoWrong.studentConfused: Go back to maman/papa only, add one new word
whenThingsGoWrong.familyStructureQuestion: Emphasize 'people who love and care for us'
whenThingsGoWrong.tooManyWords: Choose one new word (frère OR sœur) and practice well

lessons.closing: Students point to family members in photos and name them in French
lessons.realWorldConnection: Children can describe who lives in their house

lessons.title: Ma famille à moi
lessons.oneGoal: Students can point to and name their family members in photos or drawings
lessons.openingConnection: We know frère, sœur, maman, papa - now let's talk about YOUR special family!

mainActivity.description: Personalized family sharing with possessive language
activities: Introduce 'mon papa' and 'ma maman' with personal photos
Practice pointing: 'mon frère' or 'ma sœur'
Add grand-papa with gesture of wise, loving grandfather
Students create personal family poster with labels
Gallery walk where students share 'ma famille'
visualSupports: Hand gestures showing possession (pointing to self, then family)
Visual cue cards for 'mon' (masculine) vs 'ma' (feminine)
Student family photos arranged on personal posters

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for possessive words?
decisionPoints.ifReady: Practice mon/ma with multiple family members
decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Just use names without possessives: 'papa' instead of 'mon papa'

decisionPoints.question: Do some students need help with family photos?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide drawing materials and help students draw family
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on labeling and sharing existing photos

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on speaking or pointing today?
decisionPoints.ifSpeaking: Encourage students to name family members aloud
decisionPoints.ifPointing: Allow quiet pointing with teacher saying words

materials: French family labels to cut out
Crayons for students who want to draw

whenThingsGoWrong.studentEmbarrassed: Let them work with a partner or just point quietly
whenThingsGoWrong.confusedByPossessive: Skip mon/ma and just use family member names
whenThingsGoWrong.noFamilyInfo: Help student create 'chosen family' with caring adults

lessons.closing: Students hold up their family poster and say one family member name
lessons.realWorldConnection: Children show family photos and talk about them

lessons.title: Les familles sont différentes
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand that families can look different and that's wonderful
lessons.openingConnection: Look at all our family posters! Every family is different and special!

mainActivity.description: Celebrating family diversity with visual exploration
activities: Gallery walk of diverse family photos showing different structures
Practice 'différent' with contrasting family photos (size, composition)
Teach 'spécial' with heart gestures - every family is special
Learn 'beau' (beautiful) while looking at all family types
Students find similarities AND differences in family photos
Create class book page: 'Our families are different and beautiful'
visualSupports: Photo collection: single parents, grandparents raising children, mixed race families, adopted families, same-gender parents, big and small families
Heart gesture for 'spécial'
Beauty gesture (hands to face, smile) for 'beau'
Comparison charts showing different family structures

decisionPoints.question: How can I represent diverse family structures sensitively?
decisionPoints.ifSensitively: Present all families as loving, use inclusive language naturally
decisionPoints.ifQuestion: Answer simply: 'Some families have two moms, some have grandparents, all families love each other'

decisionPoints.question: Do students need time to process differences?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Slow down, let students ask questions and explore photos longer
decisionPoints.ifNo: Continue with vocabulary and move to similarities activity

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on similarities or differences today?
decisionPoints.ifSimilarities: Emphasize how all families love and care for each other
decisionPoints.ifDifferences: Celebrate the wonderful variety in family structures

materials: Diverse family photo collection (many different structures)

whenThingsGoWrong.studentQuestions: Answer simply: 'Families are made of people who love each other'
whenThingsGoWrong.confusionAboutDifferences: Focus on 'love' being the same in all families
whenThingsGoWrong.sensitiveFamilyIssue: Privately affirm that student's family is wonderful and special

lessons.closing: Students look at their own family poster and say 'Ma famille est spéciale'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Families come in many forms - single parents, grandparents, step-families, adopted families

lessons.title: Qu'est-ce qu'on fait ensemble?
lessons.oneGoal: Students can identify one activity they do with family members
lessons.openingConnection: Beautiful! All families are spécial. Now let's learn what families DO together!

mainActivity.description: Family activities introduction with action and movement
activities: Introduce 'manger' with eating gesture and family meal photos
Practice 'jouer' with play actions and game photos
Learn 'regarder' with looking gesture and TV/book photos
Family activity charades - students act out activities
Students draw one activity they do with their family
Share drawings: 'Je... avec ma famille' (with gestures)
visualSupports: Action photos: families eating together, playing games, watching movies, reading books
Large gesture cards for each activity
TPR actions: eating motion, playing motion, watching motion

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for action words?
decisionPoints.ifReady: Add all three activities and let students practice with movement
decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Focus on just one activity (manger) and do it well

decisionPoints.question: Do students need to act out activities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include lots of TPR and movement with each vocabulary word
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus more on photo recognition and simple repetition

decisionPoints.question: Should I use family activity photos?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Show diverse families doing activities together
decisionPoints.ifNo: Have students demonstrate activities with their own gestures

materials: Simple activity props (play food, books, games)

whenThingsGoWrong.tooMuchMovement: Switch to seated gestures and quiet photo activity
whenThingsGoWrong.vocabularyOverload: Choose one activity word and practice it thoroughly
whenThingsGoWrong.studentNoIdeas: Show photo prompts and help student choose one activity

lessons.closing: Students do one activity gesture and say the French word
lessons.realWorldConnection: Families eat meals together, play games, watch movies

lessons.title: Notre maison
lessons.oneGoal: Students can name where their family lives and spends time
lessons.openingConnection: Families manger, jouer, regarder - now WHERE do families do these things?

mainActivity.description: Family homes and rooms exploration with inclusive housing types
activities: Introduce 'maison' with house gesture and diverse home photos
Show 'cuisine' with cooking gesture and kitchen photos
Learn 'salon' with relaxing gesture and living room photos
Students draw their home and label one room in French
Room connection activity: match activities to rooms
Students share: 'Dans ma cuisine, on manger'
visualSupports: Diverse home photos: houses, apartments, condos, mobile homes, different sizes
Room photos showing different home layouts and decorating styles
Simple house outline template for drawing
Activity-room matching cards

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand home vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Continue with room names and matching activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus only on 'maison' and let students show their homes

decisionPoints.question: Should I include apartments and other homes?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Show apartments, condos, different types of housing naturally
decisionPoints.ifSensitive: Focus on 'home is where family is' rather than house types

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to describe rooms?
decisionPoints.ifReady: Let students describe what happens in each room
decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Just name rooms and point to them in pictures

materials: Diverse housing photos (houses, apartments, different styles)
Room photos with families doing activities

whenThingsGoWrong.housingInsecurity: Emphasize 'where family is together' not type of house
whenThingsGoWrong.vocabularyConfusion: Focus on just 'maison' and let students draw
whenThingsGoWrong.drawingDifficulty: Provide simple house templates or let students use photos

lessons.closing: Students point to their house drawing and say 'Ma maison'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Families live in houses, apartments, different types of homes

lessons.title: Nos traditions familiales
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand that families have special traditions and celebrations
lessons.openingConnection: In our maisons, families do special things! Let's learn about traditions!

mainActivity.description: Family traditions exploration celebrating cultural diversity
activities: Introduce 'tradition' with photos of diverse family celebrations
Learn 'fête' with party gesture and celebration photos
Practice 'célébrer' with happy celebration movements
Share diverse cultural traditions: birthdays, holidays, cultural festivals, special meals
Students draw or share one family tradition
Create tradition gallery showing class diversity
visualSupports: Photos of diverse cultural celebrations: Christmas, Hanukkah, Eid, Diwali, Chinese New Year, birthdays, quinceañeras, powwows, etc.
Celebration gestures (clapping, arms up, happy movements)
Cultural food photos, music, decorations from different traditions

decisionPoints.question: How can I include diverse cultural traditions?
decisionPoints.ifInclude: Show many different cultural celebrations as equally wonderful
decisionPoints.ifLimited: Start with birthdays and common celebrations, expand later

decisionPoints.question: Do students need examples of traditions first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Show lots of different tradition photos before asking students to share
decisionPoints.ifNo: Let students share their traditions and support with French vocabulary

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on holidays or daily traditions?
decisionPoints.ifHolidays: Celebrate big cultural holidays and religious celebrations
decisionPoints.ifDaily: Focus on daily traditions like family dinner, bedtime stories

whenThingsGoWrong.culturalSensitivity: Present all traditions as wonderful, avoid comparisons
whenThingsGoWrong.studentNoTraditions: Help identify simple traditions like family dinner
whenThingsGoWrong.overwhelmingChoices: Focus on one tradition student wants to share

lessons.closing: Students make celebration gesture and say 'Ma famille célèbre'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Families celebrate birthdays, holidays, have special meals and customs

lessons.title: Mon histoire familiale
lessons.oneGoal: Students can tell one simple story about their family
lessons.openingConnection: Our families have beautiful traditions! Now let's tell stories about our families!

mainActivity.description: Family storytelling with sequence support and visual aids
activities: Introduce 'histoire' with story book gesture and family story photos
Learn 'hier' (yesterday) with backward gesture and past photos
Practice 'aujourd'hui' (today) with present gesture and current photos
Teacher models simple family story with photos: 'Hier, ma famille...'
Students choose family memory to share (with photo or drawing support)
Partner storytelling with simple French phrases and gestures
visualSupports: Story sequence cards showing family activities over time
Time gesture cards: yesterday (backward point), today (here point)
Family memory photo prompts
Simple story starter phrases on cards

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to sequence events?
decisionPoints.ifReady: Help students put family memories in hier/aujourd'hui order
decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Just focus on one family memory with 'histoire' vocabulary

decisionPoints.question: Do students need story prompts or pictures?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide family activity picture prompts and story starters
decisionPoints.ifNo: Let students choose their own family memory to share

decisionPoints.question: Should stories be about recent or past events?
decisionPoints.ifRecent: Focus on yesterday and today activities
decisionPoints.ifPast: Allow any family memory that's important to student

whenThingsGoWrong.studentNonverbal: Let student point to pictures and teacher narrates in French
whenThingsGoWrong.difficultMemory: Guide toward positive, simple family activities
whenThingsGoWrong.timeConfusion: Skip time words, focus just on family 'histoire'

lessons.closing: Students show their memory picture and say 'Mon histoire'
lessons.realWorldConnection: People tell stories about their families and share memories

lessons.title: Je décris ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students can use simple descriptive words about family members
lessons.openingConnection: We have family stories! Now let's describe our family members!

mainActivity.description: Family description practice with inclusive, positive language
activities: Introduce 'grand' with tall gesture and photos of tall family members
Practice 'petit' with small gesture and photos of young family members
Learn 'gentil' (kind) with heart gesture and photos of caring moments
Students practice describing family photos: 'Mon papa est grand'
Create family description cards with drawings and labels
Guess the family member game using descriptions
visualSupports: Family photos showing different sizes and ages positively
Size comparison gestures (tall, short) that are respectful
Kindness photos: hugging, helping, caring family moments
Description word cards with pictures and gestures

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for descriptive language?
decisionPoints.ifReady: Add more descriptive words and encourage full descriptions
decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Focus on just one descriptor per family member

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on physical or personality traits?
decisionPoints.ifPhysical: Use grand/petit respectfully for height/age descriptions
decisionPoints.ifPersonality: Focus on gentil and other positive personality words

decisionPoints.question: Do students need vocabulary cards for support?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide picture-word cards for descriptive vocabulary
decisionPoints.ifNo: Let students practice descriptions from memory

materials: Diverse family photos showing different sizes, ages
Drawing materials for family description cards
Family member photos for guessing game

whenThingsGoWrong.negativeDescriptions: Redirect to positive traits, model kind language
whenThingsGoWrong.sizeSensitivity: Focus on age rather than size if needed
whenThingsGoWrong.vocabularyOverload: Choose one descriptive word and practice well

lessons.closing: Students show family photo and share one positive description
lessons.realWorldConnection: When we talk about family, we describe what they look like and how they act

lessons.title: Les émotions en famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students can express how family makes them feel
lessons.openingConnection: We describe our families! Now let's share how our families make us feel!

mainActivity.description: Family emotions exploration with emotional safety and support
activities: Introduce 'heureux' (happy) with big smile and happy family photos
Practice 'content' (pleased/satisfied) with calm happy gesture
Learn 'aimé' (loved) with hug-self gesture and loving family photos
Students match emotion words to family activity photos
Create feeling flower: family activities that make them feel each emotion
Share: 'Avec ma famille, je suis...' with emotion gesture
visualSupports: Family emotion photos: laughing together, hugging, playing peacefully
Emotion face cards showing happy, content, loved feelings
Feeling flower template with petals for different emotions
Gesture cards for each emotion word

decisionPoints.question: Are students comfortable sharing emotions?
decisionPoints.ifComfortable: Encourage detailed sharing about family feelings
decisionPoints.ifNotComfortable: Keep sharing private or with just teacher

decisionPoints.question: Do students need emotion cards or faces?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide emotion face cards and let students point to feelings
decisionPoints.ifNo: Let students express emotions through gestures and words

decisionPoints.question: Should I include challenging emotions too?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Acknowledge that families sometimes have sad moments too
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus only on positive family emotions today

materials: Crayons and markers for flower activity

whenThingsGoWrong.studentSadness: Acknowledge feelings, focus on love and support available
whenThingsGoWrong.emotionalOverwhelm: Move to simple pointing activity with emotion cards
whenThingsGoWrong.familyDifficulties: Emphasize that all families have challenges and love

lessons.closing: Students hug themselves and say 'Je suis aimé dans ma famille'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Families make us feel loved, happy, safe, and sometimes other emotions too

lessons.title: Créer notre livre de famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students begin creating a simple family book with pictures and words
lessons.openingConnection: Family emotions are beautiful! Let's create a book about our families!

mainActivity.description: Family book creation project with scaffolded writing support
activities: Introduce 'livre' with book gesture and family book examples
Practice 'page' by turning pages and pointing
Learn 'écrire' (to write) with writing gesture and examples
Students plan their family book: what to include on each page
Create first book page: cover with 'Ma Famille' and decorations
Choose photos or draw family members for inside pages
visualSupports: Family book examples showing different styles and contents
Book-making materials clearly organized
Page planning template with picture/word spaces
French word labels available for students to copy

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for a creation project?
decisionPoints.ifReady: Let students plan and create their own book design
decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Provide more structure and template pages

decisionPoints.question: Do students need templates or can they start from scratch?
decisionPoints.ifTemplate: Provide book page templates with spaces for pictures and words
decisionPoints.ifScratch: Let creative students design their own book layout

decisionPoints.question: Should I focus on pictures or words today?
decisionPoints.ifPictures: Emphasize family photos and drawings with minimal writing
decisionPoints.ifWords: Help students copy French family vocabulary into books

materials: Stapler or brad fasteners for binding

whenThingsGoWrong.overwhelmedByChoices: Provide simple 3-page template: cover, family members, activities
whenThingsGoWrong.perfectionistConcerns: Emphasize that all books are beautiful and personal
whenThingsGoWrong.writingDifficulty: Let students dictate to teacher or copy simple French words

lessons.closing: Students hold their book cover and say 'Mon livre de famille'
lessons.realWorldConnection: People create photo albums and books to remember and share family memories

lessons.title: Mon arbre généalogique

mainActivity.description: Family tree creation with inclusive, diverse family structures

Show family tree examples with different family structures
Students create their own family tree using template or freehand
Add family photos or drawings to their tree
visualSupports: Family tree examples showing single parents, grandparents, step-families, adopted families, etc.
Tree templates with flexible branching for different family structures
Family relationship picture cards
Examples of creative family trees (not just traditional format)

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand family relationships?

decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on immediate family members (people at home) only

decisionPoints.question: Should I provide tree templates?

decisionPoints.ifNo: Let students draw their own tree design from scratch

decisionPoints.question: How can I accommodate different family structures?
decisionPoints.ifAccommodate: Show trees with guardians, single parents, blended families as equally valid
decisionPoints.ifSensitive: Focus on 'important people in my family' rather than traditional roles

materials: Large paper for creative tree designs
Green paper for leaves, brown for branches

whenThingsGoWrong.complexFamilySituation: Help student focus on people who care for them now
whenThingsGoWrong.traditionalTreeDoesntFit: Create 'family garden' or 'family heart' instead of tree

lessons.closing: Students point to their family tree and say 'Mon arbre de famille'
lessons.realWorldConnection: Family trees help people understand how family members are related

lessons.title: Partager nos familles

mainActivity.description: Presentation preparation with confidence-building supports

Students practice presenting with their family books and trees
Partner practice: students share with one other person first

visualSupports: Presentation example videos or photos of children sharing
Gesture cards for presenting vocabulary
Simple French phrases for presentations on chart
Visual cues for good presentation skills

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to share publicly?

decisionPoints.ifNotReady: Keep sharing in pairs or small groups for comfort

decisionPoints.question: Do students need presentation supports?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide French phrase cards and presentation structure supports
decisionPoints.ifNo: Let students present freely using vocabulary they know

decisionPoints.question: Should sharing be in pairs or small groups?
decisionPoints.ifPairs: Continue partner sharing for more practice and comfort
decisionPoints.ifGroups: Move to small group sharing (3-4 students) for safety

materials: Students' family books and trees from previous lessons

whenThingsGoWrong.presentationAnxiety: Allow written sharing or drawing instead of speaking
whenThingsGoWrong.studentNotReady: Let student be audience member only, no pressure
whenThingsGoWrong.vocabularyForgotten: Provide phrase cards and pointing supports

lessons.closing: Students practice presentation opening: 'Voici ma famille'

mainActivity.description: Culminating family celebration with presentations and reflection

Introduce 'apprendre' (to learn) with learning gesture and examples
Students present their family books and trees to class
Celebration of family diversity: all families are wonderful

Photo documentation of student presentations
Celebration music from different cultures

decisionPoints.question: Are students confident enough to present?

decisionPoints.question: Should presentations be formal or informal?

decisionPoints.ifInformal: Casual sharing in circle with family books and trees displayed

decisionPoints.question: How can I ensure every family feels celebrated?

decisionPoints.ifWorried: Prepare inclusive language celebrating all family structures equally

whenThingsGoWrong.studentRefusesPresent: Let them show their work quietly to teacher only
whenThingsGoWrong.timeRunsOut: Continue celebration over multiple days if needed

lessons.closing: Group celebration: 'Nos familles sont belles et spéciales!'

Create album pages with photos and French descriptions
Add family vocabulary labels to photos
Decorate album pages with family traditions and cultural elements
Partner sharing of photo albums with French descriptions
